This tutorial documents the continuum models used in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) and twisted transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) moiré systems.

Section 1 — Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) Continuum Model

Introduction

Physics

The TBG continuum model (Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011)) Hamiltonian near valley \(K\) is:

\[ H_K = \begin{pmatrix} h_+(\mathbf{k}) & T(\mathbf{r}) \\ T^\dagger(\mathbf{r}) & h_-(\mathbf{k}) \end{pmatrix} \]

Usage

Key parameters:

Parameter Typical value Description
\(\theta\) 1.05° (magic) Twist angle

Code

TBG continuum model

import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import eigh

## Section 1 — Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) Continuum Model

### Introduction


### Physics

The TBG continuum model (@bistritzer_moire_2011) Hamiltonian near valley $K$ is:

$$
H_K = \begin{pmatrix}
h_+(\mathbf{k}) & T(\mathbf{r}) \\
T^\dagger(\mathbf{r}) & h_-(\mathbf{k})
\end{pmatrix}
$$

### Usage


**Key parameters:**

| Parameter | Typical value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta$ | 1.05° (magic) | Twist angle |


### Code

**TBG continuum model**

```python
import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import eigh
```
